description.narrative: IFC proposes to invest upto US$200 million in Piramal Finance Limited (PFL or the Company), erstwhile known as Piramal Capital Housing Finance Limited (PCHFL). IFCs investment will be structured as a senior, secured US$ loan under the External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) route. Additionally, IFC will help the Company mobilize up to US$150 million from other external commercial lenders. IFCs loan proceeds will be deployed towards the following segments: (i) affordable housing loans and (ii) loans to micro and small enterprises (MSEs). At least 60 percent of the IFC loan proceeds will be towards women affordable housing homeowners/co-owners or women-owned MSEs (WMSEs). At least 10 percent of the IFC loan proceeds will be deployed in the low-income state of Uttar Pradesh (UP) for affordable housing or MSE loans.

Increased Access to affordable housing finance, including for women borrowers: IFC anticipates that the Project will support increased access to affordable housing finance, especially for women borrowers. Rapid urbanization in India and the lack of affordable housing finance have led to several challenges such as congestion, pressure on basic amenities and significant shortage of housing in cities, especially in the affordable segment. Recent estimates suggest Indias urban housing demand (including existing shortages) by 2030 will be 31.2 million units of which approximately 68 percent will be for affordable housing units. The estimated market size for womens housing loans in India is US$32.3 billion, largely comprising of demand for apartments (84 percent) as per IFCs Her Home Housing Finance for Women 2019 Report. Access of women borrowers to housing finance is further constrained lack of property ownership by women, insufficient income of women and traditional gender. Increased access to finance for MSEs, including for WMSEs: IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will help increase access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India, including for women-owned MSMEs (WMSMEs). MSMEs are critical for Indias growth and contribute significantly to GDP, exports and employment. However, of the estimated 63 million MSMEs in the country, only about 25 million have availed credit from formal sources, signifying the significant gap that exists for MSME finance in the country. While credit to MSMEs is back to pre-COVID-19 levels, supported by various enabling schemes of the GoI and RBI, providing continuity in access to finance will be key to ensuring sustainable growth. Increased access to finance in the LIS of UP: IFC anticipates that the Project will help increase access to finance for MSE and affordable housing borrowers in the state of UP. In terms of MSMEs, the state of UP contributes 14 percent of the MSMEs (in count) in India.
